findings.defect: The veiling glare around the sun is a round grey ball with a visible rim: it reads as a glow sprite pasted over the frame (and over the dark Earth below the limb). Radial profile, median 8-bit luma over the upper half between the spikes, identical in the LEO limb view and the deep-space EV 12 view: 251 at 20 px, 209 at 40, 130 at 80, 82 at 120, 44 at 160, 27 at 180, 12 at 200, 3 at 220, 0 from 260 px. That is a near-linear ramp that ends in black at about 0.32 rad. Between 200 and 260 px the HDR glare falls only 2.2 x (theta^-3) while the display falls from 12/255 to 0.
findings.realReference: Photographs of the sun from orbit (ISS, Apollo Hasselblad) show a blown-out core whose glow thins out continuously and has no radius at which it stops; the faint veil usually reaches the frame edges. No circle can be traced around it.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/sky/flare.ts: a single power law for the halo (HALO_POWER = 1.5, STARBURST.haloCore 0.012 rad, FLARE_HALO_SHARE 0.55 of STARBURST.energy 0.004), evaluated in FLARE_WGSL of src/render/sky/shaders.ts (`halo = t.shape.y * pow(1.0 + x * x, -FLARE_HALO_POWER)`). The rim itself is made by the display transform: src/render/core/post/tonemap.ts (AgX plus the 'mild punchy look', extra contrast) crushes about 3.5 stops above black into about 1 stop, so any smooth tail ends abruptly. The hand-off (section 3, 'What the glare looks like on screen') describes this and leaves it.
findings.fixDirection: Two parts. Core (request to core-support): let the toe of the tonemap roll off over at least 3 stops, with no added contrast below about 4 stops under mid-grey; the same toe hides the Milky Way (see the night-sky finding). Sky: replace the single theta^-3 halo by a tight core plus a wide, weak veil falling as theta^-2 (the CIE veiling-glare law), renormalised to the same total energy, so that at the metered exposure of a sunlit scene the glare is still above 1/255 at the frame edge instead of ending inside the frame. Add a spec on the 8-bit radial profile: from the first radius where it is below 16/255 it must take at least a doubling of the radius to reach 0.

findings.defect: The diffraction starburst is 14 identical, perfectly straight hairlines at exact 25.7 degree spacing that run from the sun to the frame edges. Measured on flare-deep-space-ev12.png along the spike towards (1280, 200): peak luma 87, 52, 35, 27 over the four quarters of its length; width (pixels at 12/255 or more) 5.9, 2.3, 1.9, 1.6 px. Beyond the first quarter it is a 2 px line of constant width, still 27/255 at 700 px (33 deg) from the sun; in the 35 deg off-axis view the lines cross the whole 97 deg frame. It looks like a vector starburst icon or a 'star filter' plug-in. The lines stay equally sharp across the Earth and across the ghosts.
findings.realReference: A sunstar from a 7-blade iris is a set of tapered fans: wide and blown out at the base, fading to nothing within a few degrees (rarely more than 5-10 deg at f/16-22, absent at wide apertures), of unequal length and brightness because the blades are not identical, with visible colour dispersion along them. Nothing in a photograph is a constant-width line across the frame.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/sky/flare.ts STARBURST { spikeWidth: 0.0009 rad, spikeLength: 0.012 rad } and spikeProfile(): a Gaussian of constant angular width across the spike (sigma 0.62 px at 720p / 60 deg: sub-pixel, so only TAA holds the line together) times 1 / (1 + theta^2 / L^2) along it, with no end and no per-spike variation; (1 - FLARE_HALO_SHARE) = 45 % of the term, 0.18 % of the sun's illuminance, goes into the 14 lines. Shader: FLARE_WGSL in src/render/sky/shaders.ts (`gw`, `along`, `spikes`).
findings.fixDirection: Model the blades as slightly curved edges: let the spike's width grow with theta (w = w0 + k * theta, renormalised on the CPU as now) so that its peak falls at least as theta^-3 and it dissolves into the glare as a fan; give each of the 7 blade pairs its own amplitude and length (seeded, +-20-30 %) and a small angular irregularity; cut the spikes' share to 10-15 % of the starburst; keep sigma at or above 1 px at the render resolution. Re-take the flare views at the metered exposure (EV 14-15) as well as at EV 9-12.

findings.defect: Hard LOD pop where the impostor hands over to geometry. The sheet equalises the exposure for distance, so every tile should be equally bright. Display-linear luma integrated over the body, per tile: 7.1, 7.5, 8.6, 7.9 for the impostor tiles (0.5-4.2 px), then 0.88 at 6.6 px (9 x darker), 4.4 at 13 px, 5.5 at 21 px. At the same step the colour flips from blue-white (R:G:B 0.80 : 1 : 1.35) to neutral grey (1.05 : 1 : 0.95) and the shape from a round dot to a thin crescent (the body is at phase 125 deg; the impostor shows a full round blob). Spec log of this run: 'TAA keeps 99 % at 4.2 px, 34 % at 6.6 px, 76 % at 13.2 px, 89 % at 20.7 px'. A body growing through 4-7 px (the Moon from Earth orbit is 6-9 px at 720p-1080p; the Earth in the map view) blinks dark and changes colour.
findings.realReference: A planet approached by a camera keeps its integrated brightness and colour. A crescent 4-7 px across is already an elongated, off-centre sliver, not a round dot, and it does not dim when it first resolves.
findings.likelyCause: (a) src/render/sky/photometry.ts impostorWeight(): the fade is driven by the diameter (IMPOSTOR_FULL_PX 3, IMPOSTOR_NONE_PX 6), so a crescent whose lit width is 1.4 px is handed to geometry that the core's TAA resolve cannot hold (src/render/core/post/postProcess.ts). docs/requests/sky-lighting-1.md is now 'Status: declined' and its resolution advises handing over on lit width; the hand-off (sections 6.1, 9) still calls the request open. (b) src/render/sky/feature.ts prepareImpostors(): colour = BodyDef.render.meanColor and flux = Lambert sphere x geometricAlbedo, which the rendered body (here the lab Earth without atmosphere) does not match; impostorSigmaPx() makes the blob round at every phase.
findings.fixDirection: Follow the core-support resolution: keep the impostor at full weight until the lit width D / 2 x (1 + cos(phase)) exceeds about 2-3 px and fade over the next 2-3 px of lit width. Between about 2 and 12 px draw the analytic phase shape (lit crescent of a sphere convolved with the PSF) instead of a round Gaussian. Check colour and flux of the hand-over against the real terrain + atmosphere renderers, and replace the logged kept fraction by an assertion on the display sum across the sheet (step-to-step change under 15 %). Correct the hand-off.

findings.defect: At the darkest exposure the game can reach (dark-adapted floor, EV100 -2.9) the night sky from orbit is an almost empty black frame. leo-night-dark-adapted.png: 46 stars with a peak of 64/255 or more and 165 at 32/255 or more in the whole visible sky; the Milky Way corner averages (1.1, 1.0, 1.1)/255 and the Large Magellanic Cloud (3.2, 1.9, 4.3)/255, invisible on a normal monitor. What does show is hue-shifted: the LMC is purple, and in milky-way-band-ev-3.png the band is dark red-brown (16.9, 9.2, 6.2 = 1 : 0.54 : 0.37, against 1 : 0.81 : 0.73 for the bulge at EV -5 in starfield-deep-space-ev-5.png). The good-looking star-field screenshots are taken at EV -5, which the game never reaches (EV_MIN = -3).
findings.realReference: From the night side of an orbit a dark-adapted observer, and any ISS night photograph, sees a dense field of thousands of stars and an obvious Milky Way. Faint diffuse light looks pale grey-white (no colour at scotopic levels, low saturation in a short camera exposure), never saturated red or purple.
findings.likelyCause: Not the sky's photometry (about 5e-4 cd/m^2 for the band is right) but where it lands: src/render/core/post/exposure.ts EV_DARK_FLOOR = EV_MIN = -3 puts the Milky Way 5.6 stops below mid-grey, and src/render/core/post/tonemap.ts (AgX, minEv -12.47, plus the 'mild punchy look: a little more contrast and saturation') crushes that range to 1-5/255 and raises saturation per channel in the toe. The brief forbids a brightness knob in the sky, so the sky cannot fix it alone.
findings.fixDirection: Request to core-support: let the exposure floor fall to about EV -6 when no lit object and no emitter is in view (slow adaptation over tens of seconds, as the eye), and remove the look's extra contrast and saturation below about 4 stops under mid-grey (or desaturate the toe). Then re-take leo-night-dark-adapted and milky-way-band at the floor and require in tests/browser/sky/stars.spec.ts a Milky Way mean of at least 12/255 in Sagittarius and Crux and channel ratios within 20 % of the EV -5 image.

findings.defect: With the shipped default (Milky Way cube uploaded from 1024 per face) the faint-star layer under the catalogue stars is magnified 2.6 x in this view and turns into soft, partly oblong smudges 3-5 px across beside pin-sharp PSF stars: two visibly different kinds of star in one frame. Column autocorrelation of the background at lags 2 / 3: 0.57 / 0.27 with 1024 against 0.43 / 0.13 with 2048. The hand-off calls the cost 'invisible at a 70 deg field', but that was measured at 720p: at the 1440p target and 60 deg a pixel is 0.042 deg against a 0.088 deg texel, the same 2.1 x magnification over the whole sky in normal play (3.1 x at 4K). No lattice and no cube seam were found (no periodic autocorrelation peak; the galactic-centre view is clean at gain 4).
findings.realReference: Stars fainter than the naked-eye limit are still points: a real sky has one continuous population of points down to the noise over a smooth diffuse glow.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/sky/feature.ts loadSky(): `limit = options.milkyWayFaceSize ?? MILKY_WAY_FACE_SIZE` (1024) skips the finest baked mip to stay inside the 0.1 GB VRAM line; BACKGROUND_FS samples it bilinearly. docs/requests/sky-lighting-2.md is 'declined, escalate: lead' and undecided; the hand-off still lists it as open.
findings.fixDirection: Ship 2048 (the lead raises the line), or fit 2048 into the same memory: transcode the chain to BC6H where 'texture-compression-bc' is available (8 bits per texel against 32 for rgb9e5, so the full 2048 chain is about 34 MB, the size of today's 1024 chain) with the 1024 rgb9e5 chain as fallback. Alternatively extend the PSF catalogue to V 8.5-9 (a few tens of thousands of instances, far inside the 0.08 ms background budget) and bake those stars out of the cube, so the cube carries only diffuse light, which survives magnification.

findings.defect: The four ghosts are flat, evenly filled discs with a crisp orange-red outline (rim within about 2 px, uniform interior), exactly on one line, each in a different pastel colour: the look of a 1990s lens-flare plug-in. With the sun just outside the frame three of them hang at full strength in an otherwise black frame.
findings.realReference: Real ghosts are images of the iris: polygonal (7 sides here) or cut to a cat's eye off axis, with soft defocused edges, uneven interiors (caustic arcs, brighter cusps), very different sizes and brightnesses, usually a dozen or more of which most are barely visible.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/sky/flare.ts GHOSTS (4 entries) and ghostProfile(): `disc * (0.55 + 0.45 * smoothstep(0.6, 1, r))` with an edge of width softness x radius and a per-channel radial shift that draws the red outline; the ghost branch of FLARE_WGSL in src/render/sky/shaders.ts.
findings.fixDirection: Give the ghosts the aperture's shape (a 7-gon turned with the blades, from the same blade data as the spikes), a wider soft edge and a non-uniform interior; add more and fainter ghosts with a spread of radii (some far larger than the frame at very low luminance); clip by a second circle off axis; keep their total at or under the present 0.036 %.

findings.defect: At long exposure the star field is uniform 'salt' and the constellations do not read. In the Orion close-up Betelgeuse (V 0.5) and Rigel (V 0.1) are 5.5 px blobs (23-24 px at 128/255 or more), the belt stars 4.5 px (15-16 px), ordinary V 4-6 stars 1-4 px; alpha and beta Centauri in the Crux view are hardly larger than their neighbours. Bright stars get no glare at all while the sun, through the same lens, gets a 200 px halo and 14 spikes: the lens model is inconsistent between features.
findings.realReference: In a photograph of Orion at this field the two first-magnitude stars dominate: saturated discs several times wider than the faint stars with a soft glow around them (lens glare, halation) that keeps the star's colour (Betelgeuse orange).
findings.likelyCause: src/render/sky/photometry.ts STAR_PSF_SIGMA_PX = 0.7 and STARS_WGSL in src/render/sky/shaders.ts: a pure Gaussian has no wings, so the visible radius grows only as sqrt(ln(flux)). The glare function of the lens (flare.ts haloProfile) is applied to the sun only.
findings.fixDirection: Give point sources the same lens: add to the star PSF (and to the impostors) the normalised glare profile of flare.ts at its energy fraction (about 0.2 % of the star's flux, taken out of the core so the total stays E / Omega_px), drawn on a larger quad only for the few dozen stars whose glare exceeds 1/255 at the frame's exposure. That is photometry, not a brightness knob, and the PSF photometry spec keeps holding.

findings.view: C:/dev/fable-space-game/out/screens/sky/pbr-spheres-leo-day.png (chrome sphere, x 660-790, y 300-420; the black glossy sphere left of it)
findings.defect: In the chrome sphere the Earth's reflection carries a broken, dashed white line along the horizon and isolated white specks below it (single probe texels) beside a blurred, blocky Earth. The same line shows as a faint seam across the black glossy sphere.
findings.realReference: A mirror ball above a cloudy Earth shows a continuous bright limb band and smooth cloud fields, no sparkle.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/sky/shaders.ts PROBE_FACE_CS coverageAt(): `textureSampleLevel(cloudCoverageMapTex, linearRepeat, uv, 0.0)` point-samples the 8192 x 4096 coverage map (4.9 km texels) once per probe texel, whose footprint is 5 km at the nadir from 200 km and hundreds of km towards the limb. The albedo lookup beside it is footprint-matched (`lod` in bodyRadiance); the cloud lookup is not. The cube is rebuilt every 12 frames while the vessel moves about 1.5 km, so the specks should also crawl (not verifiable from stills).
findings.fixDirection: Sample the coverage with the same footprint LOD as the albedo (needs mips on 'clouds.coverageMap': request to atmosphere-clouds / core-support), or average 4-8 taps spread over the texel's footprint; add a probe spec that compares a limb texel with the mean coverage over its footprint.

findings.view: C:/dev/fable-space-game/out/screens/sky/leo-night-dark-adapted.png (a still cannot show it; the evidence is the log of tests/browser/sky/stars.spec.ts 'static camera' in this run)
findings.defect: Stars shimmer for a static camera in vacuum. Log of this run: 'resolved (TAA), 515 star pixels above 0.05: consecutive frames differ by 0.82 % on average, 7.5 % at most; same jitter phase 8 frames apart: 2.81 % at most', a 7.5 Hz ripple on the rim pixels of every star (the builder measured up to 11/255). The acceptance criterion (frame difference zero) is still not met and the spec asserts the failing behaviour (mean < 3 %, max < 15 %).
findings.realReference: Outside an atmosphere stars are perfectly steady.
findings.likelyCause: A sigma 0.7 px Gaussian under the core's jittered 3 x 3 reconstruction (src/render/core/post/postProcess.ts). docs/requests/sky-lighting-1.md was declined; its resolution names the mitigation inside this package (a sigma of 1.0 px or more halves the ripple) and it has not been applied.
findings.fixDirection: Raise STAR_PSF_SIGMA_PX (src/render/sky/photometry.ts) to about 1.0 px (flux unchanged, peaks halve, so re-measure the '100 brightest visible' criterion together with the night-sky finding), re-measure the ripple, tighten the spec's bound to the new measurement, and correct the hand-off.

findings.defect: On the lunar surface the chrome sphere is a two-tone ball: black above a soft horizon and below it a perfectly uniform slab of (54, 54, 56) with no shading, no shadow of the spheres and no texture, while the ground it stands over is (97, 93, 86): the reflection is clearly darker and colder than the terrain it reflects. The shadowed undersides of the white and grey spheres take the same cold tint (41, 41.5, 43.5) from a warm ground.
findings.realReference: A mirror surface on the Moon (Apollo visors, foil) shows the ground at the brightness and warm grey of the ground around it, brighter towards the anti-solar point (opposition surge), with the object's own shadow in it.
findings.likelyCause: Partly the lab: the ground cap in labs/sky/main.ts uses BodyDef meanColor (0.12, 0.115, 0.105) while the probe uses the tile set's albedoLowRes, which at the landing site (0.67 N, 23.47 E) decodes to (0.064, 0.066, 0.074): darker, and blue above red, which no lunar soil is (check data/tiles/moon/globals/albedo-lowres.png and the bake's colour balance; bake-moon-sky owns it). Partly the probe: bodyRadiance() in src/render/sky/shaders.ts lights every body as a Lambert sphere (`e * albedo / PI`) without the regolith phase function the terrain renderer uses.
findings.fixDirection: Re-take this view on the real terrain renderer (lead integration) and compare the chrome reflection with the ground beside it (ratio within 20 %, same hue). If the mismatch stays, evaluate the terrain's photometric function for airless bodies per probe texel (sun and view directions are known there) and have the albedo map's colour checked against the tiles.

findings.defect: Four of the package's reviewed views are rendered over the lab stand-in Earth: flat green and blue fills, blurred blocky cloud blobs with dark outlines, no atmosphere, no limb glow. They look like placeholder art at a glance, and the package's hero shot (sun above the limb with flare) has therefore never been seen with an atmosphere: no scattering around the sun, no extinction of the disc or the flare, no blue limb in the probe reflections. Three files in the folder are not written by the functional specs and stayed at 2026-11-10 19:13 after this re-run (perf-1440p-leo-horizon.png and the two milky-way-1024-vs-2048-*-crop-3x.png); all 23 functional specs passed.
findings.realReference: Sunrise from orbit: a thin blue-to-orange limb, the sun's disc reddened and flattened at the limb, glare partly seen through air.
findings.likelyCause: labs/sky/main.ts (LabPlanet backdrop and the clouds=1 stand-in); render packages may not import each other, so the integration is left to the lead (hand-off section 7).
findings.fixDirection: Lead / integration: re-take sun-at-earth-limb, pbr-spheres-leo-day and leo-night in labs/integration with terrain, atmosphere-clouds and ocean registered and judge the flare, the probe reflections and the stars' extinction there; let a spec regenerate the comparison crops.
